title: Go SDK: extract Redwood request id and attach structured logging fields
author: Ibrahim Khan
release_notes: - Go SDK now exposes Redwood request IDs from responses/errors and includes them as structured log fields for easier correlation with traces/support tickets.
description: Motivation: Quickstart templates (RAG + agents) standardize on request-id propagation across logs/traces to make debugging/support workflows consistent. The Go SDK was missing parity with Python/TS: callers could only access the gateway request id by manually inspecting headers, and our built-in logger (when enabled) didn’t include a stable correlation field. This PR adds request-id extraction from responses, threads it through SDK result/error types, and attaches structured fields to the logger output. Summary of changes: (1) Extract `X-Redwood-Request-Id` (case-insensitive) from all API responses; (2) Add `RequestID` to `ResponseMeta` and to the primary SDK error type (so 4xx/5xx errors can be correlated); (3) When a logger is configured, include structured fields: `redwood.request_id`, `http.status_code`, `redwood.model` (if known), and `redwood.endpoint` (SDK route name, low-cardinality); (4) Add helpers: `RequestIDFromResponse(*http.Response) string` and `RequestIDFromError(error) string`; (5) Tests: httptest server coverage for happy-path and error-path extraction + logging assertions. Notes on conventions: We intentionally do NOT add user-provided prompt/content to logs. Request IDs are high-cardinality but expected/required for support correlation; other fields are restricted to low-cardinality values to avoid metrics/log pipeline blowups (per Observability guidance). Example usage: `resp, err := client.Chat(ctx, req); if rid := resp.Meta.RequestID; rid != "" { logger.Info("chat ok", "redwood.request_id", rid) }` and in the error case `if rid := redwood.RequestIDFromError(err); rid != "" { logger.Error("chat failed", "redwood.request_id", rid, "err", err) }`. Follow-ups (out of scope): add explicit OTel span attribute `redwood.request_id` once the Go SDK tracing middleware lands; and align error taxonomy strings with template error codes after the next template cut.

conversation: Monica Patel (review): Can we confirm the header name we want to standardize on? Templates mention "request_id" but I want to ensure we match the gateway. Also, please avoid logging full URLs if they include query strings. Ibrahim Khan (author): Gateway sets `X-Redwood-Request-Id` today (also forwards `X-Request-Id` from certain proxies, but not guaranteed). This PR only extracts `X-Redwood-Request-Id`. For the endpoint field I used a route enum (e.g., `chat.completions`, `embeddings.create`) rather than URL strings. Monica Patel: Great. Please add a helper to retrieve request id from wrapped errors; templates often do `errors.Is/As`. Ibrahim Khan: Added `RequestIDFromError(err)` which walks `errors.As` for `*APIError` and returns the field. Allison Grant (review): Field names: prefer `redwood.request_id` over `request_id` and keep `redwood.model` optional. Also, we should not add any per-request dynamic fields beyond request_id. Ibrahim Khan: Updated structured fields to `redwood.request_id`, `redwood.endpoint`, `http.status_code`, optional `redwood.model`. No additional dynamic fields. Caleb Johnson (review): Tests look good. One request: ensure we handle header casing and missing header gracefully (empty string). Ibrahim Khan: Added case-insensitive header lookup and explicit empty-string behavior. CI note: golangci-lint failed once due to module download timeout in runner; reran and passed. Approvals: Monica Patel approved. Allison Grant approved. Caleb Johnson approved. Merged via squash.
